title: Ministry of Minority Affair’s  Jiyo Parsi Scheme  promotes Medical Assistance, Childcare, And Elderly Care
body_text:
Since inception of Jiyo Parsi scheme in the year 2013, cumulative year-wise number of beneficiaries of Parsi Community provided with the financial assistance for treatment of infertility issues, childbearing, childbirth and Post Natal Care under the Medical components is 582.  In addition, since the year 2018-19 cumulative year-wise number of beneficiaries provided with financial assistance under the Health of Community component of the scheme is 1055.  The total expenditure incurred in the scheme since its inception is Rs. 37.43 Cr.  Total 534 births have been reported in the community since the year 2014-15.  These births have brought a ray of hope among the Parsi Community towards stabilizing their declining population.  The independent third-party evaluation studies also reported the scheme as successful in meeting its target.
The details of financial assistance provided under Medical and Health of Community components of the Scheme for the last three financial years are as under:
Sl. No. Year Medical (Cr. Rs. ) Health of Community (Cr. Rs. ) Advocacy (Cr. Rs. ) 2023-24 0.11 2.53 0.10 2024-25 0.39 2.66 0.06 2025-26 0.24 2.93 0.29
(d) To increase awareness and outreach of the scheme among the Parsi community, publicity about the scheme is undertaken. Further, several workshops /interaction sessions, registration drives, bio-authentication drives are organized. Dissemination of information regarding implementation of the Jiyo Parsi Scheme is also carried out through major Parsi newspapers on monthly basis. Under this component of the scheme no direct financial assistance is provided to the beneficiaries.
This information was given by Union Minister of Minority Affairs Shri Kiren Rijiju in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.
***
AK/MR

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Minority Affairs informed the Rajya Sabha that the Jiyo Parsi scheme, launched in 2013 to arrest the declining population of the Parsi community, has provided medical assistance to 582 beneficiaries for infertility, childbearing and post-natal care, and 1,055 beneficiaries under the Health of Community component since 2018-19. A total of 534 births have been reported since 2014-15, with cumulative expenditure of Rs. 37.43 crore. The scheme also has an Advocacy component for awareness and outreach, with year-wise financial details for the last three years provided.
enrichment.context:
The Parsi (Zoroastrian) community in India has been experiencing a sharp demographic decline for decades due to low fertility rates, late marriages, and migration, with the population having fallen from over 1 lakh in the mid-20th century to roughly 57,000-60,000 in recent censuses. The Jiyo Parsi scheme was launched in 2013 by the Ministry of Minority Affairs specifically to reverse this trend by providing medical assistance for infertility treatment and childbirth, promoting awareness through advocacy campaigns, and supporting healthcare of the elderly and vulnerable within the community. It is one of the few Government of India schemes targeted at a specific religious minority community based on demographic urgency rather than economic criteria, distinguishing it from broader minority welfare schemes like the Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram or scholarship schemes for minorities.

The scheme is significant in the context of India's minority welfare architecture, which is typically governed by the National Commission for Minorities Act and focuses on six notified minorities (Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis, and Jains). Jiyo Parsi's design—combining direct financial assistance with community outreach and third-party evaluation—reflects an evidence-based approach to population-specific interventions, and its reported success (534 births, positive third-party evaluations) is often cited in discussions on demographic policy and minority-specific welfare interventions in India.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Jiyo Parsi' scheme, implemented by the Ministry of Minority Affairs, primarily aims to:
options: Provide scholarships to Parsi students for higher education
Arrest the declining population of the Parsi community through financial and medical assistance
Preserve Parsi religious monuments and fire temples
Promote skill development among Parsi youth
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, the Jiyo Parsi scheme, launched in 2013, provides financial assistance for treatment of infertility, childbearing, childbirth and post-natal care to help stabilize the declining Parsi population.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the six communities notified as 'minorities' under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992?
prelims_questions.explanation: The six notified minority communities in India are Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis (Zoroastrians), and Jains. Marathas are not a notified minority community.

mains_questions.question: The Parsi community in India faces a demographic decline unique among its religious minorities. Discuss the objectives and components of the Jiyo Parsi scheme and evaluate its effectiveness in addressing this challenge.
